<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Epístola prima ad Corínthios
<r>1 Cor 2:1-5</r>
<n>1</n> Et ego, cum veníssem ad vos, fratres, veni non in sublimitáte sermónis, aut sapiéntiæ, annúntians vobis testimónium Christi.
<n>2</n> Non enim iudicávi me scire áliquid inter vos, nisi Iesum Christum, et hunc crucifíxum.
<n>3</n> Et ego in infirmitáte, et timóre, et tremóre multo fui apud vos:
<n>4</n> Et sermo meus, et prædicátio mea non in persuasibílibus humánæ sapiéntiæ verbis, sed in ostensióne spíritus et virtútis:
<n>5</n> Ut fides vestra non sit in sapiéntia hóminum, sed in virtúte Dei.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Illumináre, illumináre Ierúsalem, quia venit lux tua:
* Et glória Dómini super te orta est.
<r>℣.</r> Et ambulábunt gentes in lúmine tuo, et reges in splendóre ortus tui.
<r>℟.</r> Et glória Dómini super te orta est.
b.345cdbe378:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the first letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians
<r>1 Cor 2:1-5</r>
<n>1</n> And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not in loftiness of speech or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of Christ.
<n>2</n> For I judged not myself to know anything among you, but Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
<n>3</n> And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.
<n>4</n> And my speech and my preaching was not in the persuasive words of human wisdom, but in shewing of the Spirit and power;
<n>5</n> That your faith might not stand on the wisdom of men, but on the power of God.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Shine, shine, O Jerusalem, for thy light is come;
* And the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.
<r>℣.</r> And the Gentiles shall walk in thy light, and kings in the brightness of thy rising.
<r>℟.</r> And the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>1 Cor 2:6-9</r>
<n>6</n> Sapiéntiam autem lóquimur inter perféctos: sapiéntiam vero non huius sǽculi, neque príncipum huius sǽculi, qui destruúntur:
<n>7</n> Sed lóquimur Dei sapiéntiam in mystério, quæ abscóndita est, quam prædestinávit Deus ante sǽcula in glóriam nostram,
<n>8</n> Quam nemo príncipum huius sǽculi cognóvit: si enim cognovíssent, nunquam Dóminum glóriæ crucifixíssent.
<n>9</n> Sed sicut scriptum est: Quod óculus non vidit, nec auris audívit, nec in cor hóminis ascéndit, quæ præparávit Deus iis, qui díligunt illum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Omnes de Saba vénient, aurum et thus deferéntes, et laudem Dómino annuntiántes,
* Allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Reges Tharsis et ínsulæ múnera ófferent, reges Arabum et Saba dona addúcent.
<r>℟.</r> Allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.
b.00b9206b9d:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>1 Cor 2:6-9</r>
<n>6</n> Howbeit we speak wisdom among the perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, neither of the princes of this world that come to nought;
<n>7</n> But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, a wisdom which is hidden, which God ordained before the world, unto our glory
<n>8</n> Which none of the princes of this world knew; for if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.
<n>9</n> But, as it is written: That eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither hath it entered into the heart of man, what things God hath prepared for them that love him.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> All they from Saba shall come, they shall bring gold and incense, and they shall show forth the praises of the Lord.
* Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents, the kings of Arabia and Saba shall offer gifts.
<r>℟.</r> Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<r>1 Cor 2:10-13</r>
<n>10</n> Nobis autem revelávit Deus per Spíritum suum: Spíritus enim ómnia scrutátur, étiam profúnda Dei.
<n>11</n> Quis enim hóminum scit quæ sunt hóminis, nisi spíritus hóminis, qui in ipso est? ita et quæ Dei sunt, nemo cognóvit, nisi Spíritus Dei.
<n>12</n> Nos autem non spíritum huius mundi accépimus, sed Spíritum, qui ex Deo est, ut sciámus, quæ a Deo donáta sunt nobis:
<n>13</n> Quæ et lóquimur non in doctis humánæ sapiéntiæ verbis, sed in doctrína Spíritus, spirituálibus spirituália comparántes.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Magi véniunt ab Oriénte Ierosólymam, quæréntes, et dicéntes: Ubi est qui natus est, cuius stellam vídimus?
* Et vénimus adoráre Dóminum.
<r>℣.</r> Vídimus stellam eius in Oriénte.
<r>℟.</r> Et vénimus adoráre Dóminum.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Et vénimus adoráre Dóminum.
b.7275c458ed:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<r>1 Cor 2:10-13</r>
<n>10</n> But to us God hath revealed them, by this Spirit. For the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.
<n>11</n> For what man knoweth the things of a man, but the spirit of a man that is in him? So the things also that are of God no man knoweth, but the Spirit of God.
<n>12</n> Now we have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit that is of God; that we may know the things that are given us from God.
<n>13</n> Which things also we speak, not in the learned words of human wisdom; but in the doctrine of the Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> There came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, asking and saying: Where is He That is born King of the Jews? for we have seen His star in the east;
* And are come to worship the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> We have seen His star in the east.
<r>℟.</r> And are come to worship the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> And are come to worship the Lord.

b.9ed651568e:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui hodiérna die Unigénitum tuum géntibus stella duce revelásti: concéde propítius; ut qui iam te ex fide cognóvimus, usque ad contemplándam spéciem tuæ celsitúdinis perducámur.
<h>P</h>er eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio S. Hygini Papæ et Martyris</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Qui odit ánimam suam in hoc mundo, in vitam ætérnam custódit eam.

<r>℣.</r> Iustus ut palma florébit.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut cedrus Líbani multiplicábitur.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>G</c>regem tuum, Pastor ætérne, placátus inténde: et, per beátum Hygínum Mártyrem tuum atque Summum Pontíficem, perpétua protectióne custódi; quem totíus Ecclésiæ præstitísti esse pastórem.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.70bbf777fd:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who by the leading of a star didst, as on this day, manifest thine Only-begotten Son to the Gentiles, mercifully grant that we, which know thee now by faith, may after this life have the fruition of thy glorious Godhead:
<h>T</h>hrough the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoration of St. Hyginus, Pope and Martyr</r>
<r>Ant.</r> He that hateth his life in this world, shall keep it unto life eternal.

<r>℣.</r> The righteous shall flourish like the palm-tree.
<r>℟.</r> He shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.

<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>L</c>ook forgivingly on thy flock, Eternal Shepherd, and keep it in thy constant protection, by the intercession of blessed Hyginus thy Martyr and Sovereign Pontiff, whom thou didst constitute Shepherd of the whole Church.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.d841b178ff:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>P</c>rídie Idus Ianuárii Luna quarta. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ sanctæ Tatiánæ Mártyris, quæ, sub Alexándro Imperatóre, uncis atque pectínibus laniáta, béstiis expósita et in ignem missa, sed nil læsa, demum, gládio percússa, migrávit in cælum.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sanctórum Tígrii Presbýteri, et Eutrópii Lectóris; qui, Arcádii Imperatóris témpore, cum de incéndio quo Ecclésia princeps et Senátus cúria conflagráverant, tamquam per eos ad exsílium sancti Ioánnis Chrysóstomi ulciscéndum excitáto, per calúmniam accusáti essent, sub Præfécto urbis Optáto, inánium deórum superstitióne implícito et Christiánæ religiónis osóre, passi sunt.
<h>I</h>n Acháia sancti Sátyri Mártyris, qui cum ante quoddam idólum tránsiret, in illud exsufflávit, signans sibi frontem, atque statim idólum córruit; ob quam causam decollátus est.
<h>E</h>ódem die sancti Arcádii Mártyris, génere et miráculis clari.
<h>I</h>n Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Zótici, Rogáti, Modésti, Cástuli, et corónæ Mílitum quadragínta.
<h>T</h>íbure sancti Zótici Mártyris.
<h>E</h>phési pássio sanctórum quadragínta duórum Monachórum, qui ob cultum sanctárum Imáginum, sub Constantíno Coprónymo, sævíssime cruciáti, martýrium complevérunt.
<h>R</h>avénnæ sancti Ioánnis, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>V</h>erónæ sancti Probi Epíscopi.
<h>I</h>n Anglia sancti Benedícti, Abbátis et Confessóris.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.7cecf3201c:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>anuary 12th 2027, the 4th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyr Tatiana, in the persecution under the Emperor Alexander. She was lacerated with hooks and combs, thrown to wild beasts, and cast into the fire, but as she remained unhurt, was at length beheaded, and so passed away to heaven.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy martyrs Tigrius the Priest and Eutropius the Reader, who suffered in the time of the Emperor Arcadius.
<h>I</h>n the Peloponnesos, the holy martyr Satyrus. As he was passing before a certain idol he breathed upon it, and signed himself with the sign of the cross upon his own forehead, whereupon the idol straightway fell down, and for this cause Satyrus was beheaded, (in the year 267.)
<h>U</h>pon the same day, (in Morocco, in the year 259) the holy martyr Arcadius, eminent for his rank and his miracles.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Zoticus, Rogatus, Modestus, Castulus, and a crown of forty soldiers.
<h>A</h>t Tivoli, (in the year 126,) the holy martyr Zoticus.
<h>A</h>t Ephesus, forty-two holy monks, who were most cruelly tortured and suffered martyrdom under the Emperor Constantine Copronymus for the honouring of holy images.
<h>A</h>t Ravenna, the holy Confessor John, Archbishop of that see, (about the year 489.)
<h>A</h>t Verona, holy Probus, Bishop of that see, (about the year 236.)
<h>I</h>n England, (in the year 690,) the holy Confessor Benedict Biscop, founder, and Abbot of the monastery of Jarrow-upon-Tyne, whose feast we keep upon the 12th day of February.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
